description: Arbitrum One — mirrors the live HyperEVM v0.8.5 deployment (Symmio 0x57331038c21982116EE9b0906E4a5c5cB52dcE2e). Every parameter here was read from that chain: via getters where one exists, and via MAStorage storage slots where none does.

readVia: getters: balanceLimitPerUser, maxWithdrawParts, deallocateDebounceTime, muon validity (60/60)

MAStorage slots at keccak256('diamond.standard.storage.masteragreement'): deallocateCooldown, settlementCooldown, liquidatorShare, liquidationTimeout, forceCloseCooldowns, forceCancelCooldown, forceCancelCloseCooldown, pendingQuotesValidLength, maxPartyAConnectionLimit
_provenance.correction: deallocateCooldown was previously recorded as 0, read from getMinWithdrawCooldown(). That getter returns WithdrawStorage.minWithdrawCooldown, which is a DIFFERENT field with its own setter (setMinWithdrawCooldown). setDeallocateCooldown() writes MAStorage.withdrawCooldownPeriod, which is 259200 (3 days) on HyperEVM. Deploying with 0 would have let users withdraw immediately after deallocating instead of waiting 3 days.
_provenance.note: muon validity is set via MUON_UPNL_VALID_TIME / MUON_PRICE_VALID_TIME in .env, not this file

_notes.balanceLimitPerUser: Raw collateral-token units. HyperEVM collateral is 6-decimal USDC, and Arbitrum USDC is also 6 decimals, so this value ports directly. Be aware 1e24 raw = 1e18 USDC per user, i.e. effectively no cap — that is what HyperEVM runs today. The old built-in default (parseEther("10000") = 1e22) was written assuming an 18-decimal collateral and is equally meaningless against USDC; set a real number here if you want an actual limit.
_notes.deallocateCooldown: 259200 (3 days) on HyperEVM. Read from MAStorage.withdrawCooldownPeriod, which is what setDeallocateCooldown() actually writes. Do NOT read this from getMinWithdrawCooldown() — that returns WithdrawStorage.minWithdrawCooldown, a different field with its own setter, which is 0 on HyperEVM. The two are unrelated despite the similar names.
_notes.templateOrder: Template ids are assigned in array order and hedgers reference templates by id. Arbitrum's reviewed id 3 is InstantOpenNoMargin — the built-in defaults put InstantOpenWithCustomVA there instead, which would silently break hedgers expecting this layout.
